title: Additional squared length bound
statement: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b,t$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, let $L(t,c)$ be their symmetric average length. For every $c\ge0$, $L(t,c)\le\sqrt c+L(t,0)$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a real-valued function on the reals
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. For any real $t$ and $c\ge0$, $L(t,c)\le\sqrt c+L(t,0)$.
